Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
322 PM EDT Wed Aug 5 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
The Flood Watch has been cancelled with most of the activity
moving  into southeast PA. No other changes have been made to 
the forecast with the summer-like pattern continuing. 

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Daily shower and thunderstorm chances are expected through
  early next week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...

KEY MESSAGE...Daily shower and thunderstorm chances are expected
through early next week.

A deep southerly flow will continue around high pressure over 
the Atlantic, ushering plenty of moisture. PWATS will be near or
greater than 2" in the valleys with 1-2" in the mountains, 
which is about 1- 2 SD above climo. A surface trough and 
shortwave energy will trigger scattered showers/thunderstorms, 
but it should not be a washout this afternoon/evening. The main
threat will be brief heavy downpours and gusty winds. However, 
shear is on the lower side, so the probability of severe storms
is lower. If some storms train over the same area, localized 
flash flooding can occur. The pattern does favor the possibility
for training convection (cloud layer winds nearly parallel to 
low-level wind), but the coverage should be isolated. 

A similar pattern will hold on for Thursday and Friday while the 
subtropical jet strengthens to the north and west. Therefore, more 
showers and thunderstorms are likely along with the threat for 
isolated instances of flash flooding and locally damaging wind 
gusts. Hotter conditions may cause relatively steeper low-level 
lapse rates and the wind field strengthens a bit (especially 
Friday). 

A quasi-zonal flow aloft will develop for the weekend into next 
week, bringing more seasonably hot and humid conditions along with 
daily chances for showers and thunderstorms.

&&

.AVIATION /19Z WEDNESDAY THROUGH MONDAY/...
VFR conditions are expected most of the time through tonight. A
thunderstorm cannot be ruled out this afternoon/evening with the
best chance around KMRB. 

Winds shift to mainly south to southwesterly for the foreseeable 
future as a Bermuda high pressure system persists across the western 
Atlantic. Daily convective chances each afternoon and evening will 
support convective-driven restrictions. With little change in the 
upcoming pattern, this sort of forecast will likely hold for the 
next several days.


&&

.MARINE...
Small Craft Advisories could be needed for parts of the waters 
at times this week, mainly in the late afternoon to evening. 
Otherwise, winds remain around 10 knots. Daily showers and 
thunderstorms expected each afternoon this week. Special Marine 
Warnings would accompany any of the stronger thunderstorms 
capable of producing frequent lightning and wind gusts over 35 
knots.


&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Anomalies climb late this week in response to return southerly 
flow. Periods of coastal flooding are possible at times of high 
tide at sensitive locations.

&&

.LWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
DC...None.
MD...None. 
VA...None.
WV...None.
MARINE...Small Craft Advisory until 8 PM EDT this evening for ANZ533-
     534-543.

&&

$$
